children: Sunil D’Souza will succeed Noel Tata as chairman from 12 November, while Jayant Balan is set to take over as managing director in May 2027

Voltas has appointed Sunil D’Souza as its next chairman, succeeding Noel N. Tata, who will step down from the position on November 11, 2026. D’Souza’s appointment will take effect from 12 November, marking a leadership transition at the Tata Group’s air-conditioning and engineering company.

The decision was taken at a board meeting on 6 November. Noel Tata, who has been associated with Voltas’s board since 2003, will retire as chairman and director in accordance with Tata Group’s superannuation guidelines. The company has appointed him Chairman Emeritus from 12 November.
D’Souza, who is already a director on Voltas’s board, will assume the chairmanship while continuing as managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Consumer Products.

He took charge of Tata Consumer Products in April 2020. Before joining the company, D’Souza served as managing director of Whirlpool India for nearly five years, overseeing its operations in India and neighbouring markets.

He previously spent close to 15 years at PepsiCo, holding commercial and general management positions across India and other Asian markets, including the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia. He began his career at Hindustan Unilever in 1993, working in sales, after starting out as a service engineer at Siemens.
D’Souza holds a bachelor's degree in electronics and communications engineering from the University of Madras and a postgraduate management diploma from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta.
Separately, Voltas has announced a succession plan for its managing director position. Current managing director C.P. Mukundan Menon will retire on 24 May 2027.

Jayant Balan, currently heading Voltas’s room air-conditioner business, will succeed him from 25 May 2027, for a five-year term, subject to shareholder approval. He will serve as managing director designate until taking charge.
The company has also appointed Venkatesalu Palaniswamy, former managing director of Trent, as an additional non-independent, non-executive director with effect from 12 November.

The leadership changes come alongside Voltas’s latest quarterly performance. The company reported a 53.5 per cent increase in quarterly profit to Rs 526.4 million, while revenue rose 10.9 per cent to Rs 25.68 billion. Its unitary cooling products business, which includes room air conditioners, recorded 29 per cent revenue growth.
Noel Tata’s exit from Voltas’s chairmanship follows his retirement as vice chairman and director of jewellery maker Titan Company on 5 November.
